ui_bugs.issue: When Upstox position returns avg_price=0 (BPCL, AARTIIND, FIVESTAR, KALYANKJIL, HINDPETRO observed), the cell computes target=0*1.05=0 and stop=0*0.97=0, so distance vs LTP is always -100% → renders 'HIT +100.00% @ ₹0.00' (green) on target and '-100.00% @ ₹0.00' (red) on stop. Misleading. Suggest suppressing the distance cell (render '—') when buy_price/avg <= 0, OR use position.last_price as fallback only when symbol is in swingMap so only real swing rows show distances.

rca of the issue: DistanceCell renders misleading '+100% / -100%' for non-swing positions because: (1) PositionsTable computes targetPrice/stopPrice via fallback `avg * (1 + target_pct/100)` and `avg * (1 - stop_pct/100)`. (2) When Upstox returns avg_price=0 (which happens for some intraday positions and on T+0 fills before settlement), targetPrice and stopPrice both compute to 0. (3) DistanceCell then computes distPct = (target_or_stop - ltp) / ltp * 100, giving -100% for both. (4) For target kind, distPct<=0 → green 'HIT +100%'. For stop kind, distPct<=0 → red 'HIT -100%'. Mitigation: in HoldingsTable / PositionsTable, before invoking DistanceCell, check `if (!swing && (avg <= 0 || !avg)) render '—'`. Or simpler: only render cells when `swingMap[sym]` exists, since percentages without a real exit anchor aren't actionable.
